thesis: CRH plc is a global building materials company (aggregates, cement, asphalt, and building products) listed on the NYSE with an Irish parent and primary U.S. operating footprint. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was **$37.45 billion** per `investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260218_rpt20251231_acc0001628280_26_009043.htm`. **[Fact]** FY2025 net income attributable to shareholders was **$3.75 billion** (diluted EPS **$5.51**) on the same filing. **[Fact]** The group reports through an Americas division (materials and building solutions) and an International division (international solutions), per segment disclosures in the FY2025 10-K and the October 2025 prospectus supplement (`424B5_20251007_rpt_acc0001193125_25_233453.htm`).
why_market_wrong: The stock may trade as a passive infrastructure beneficiary while owner cash is already capital-intensive and levered. **[Inference]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$5.62 billion** against capital spending of **$2.71 billion**, yet long-term debt on the March 2026 balance sheet was **$16.07 billion** per `10-Q_20260430_rpt20260331_acc0001628280_26_028556.htm`, so equity holders may underweight refinancing and integration risk from serial acquisitions. **[Inference]** Proof-first owner-earnings math at **$99.95** per share (July 2026 price in `valuation.json`) implies mid-single-digit negative annual returns on the automated base bridge even as reported earnings grow, suggesting the market prices reinvestment quality above what the conservative template captures. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 trailing normalized owner earnings (**$2.99 billion**) sit only modestly above the low-case anchor (**$2.91 billion**), while Q3 2025 trailing owner earnings (**$2.61 billion**) were below that anchor, so cyclical seasonality may be misread as steady compounder growth.
